summary: William M. Bodiford is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Kansas, Yale, Komazawa, and Tsukuba, he held posts at Meiji Gakuin and Iowa before becoming Professor at UCLA around 1992.

William M. Gorvine is a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Connecticut College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under David Germano in 2006.

William Magee specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held a professorship there around 1992, and later taught at Dharma Drum Buddhist College and Chung-Hwa Institute.

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) was a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Chicago, he held posts at Princeton, UCLA, and the University of Pennsylvania.

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and held academic posts at Denison University and the University of Chicago.
William Robertson (1721–1793) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1735 to 1741 and later held a post there from around 1762 to 1793.
William Roxburgh (1751–1815) studied at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Aberdeen. In 1793, he directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

William S.-Y. Wang is a linguist and sinologist. He studied at Columbia University and the University of Michigan before holding posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1966–1994) and Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2004).
William Stede (1882–1958) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of London from around 1928 to 1949.

William Theodore de Bary (1919–2017) was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia and Harvard universities, later serving as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia from around 1953 to 1990.

William Van Gordon is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2015, he was a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887) and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1882–1887).
William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He completed his studies at Lycée Condorcet (~1868–1871) and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873).

William Wright (1830–1889) was a scholar of linguistics and religion who studied at the University of St Andrews. He held posts at University College London, the British Museum, and the University of Cambridge, including Adams Professor of Arabic.

Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Jacobi at the University of Bonn from ~1904 to 1908. He succeeded Jacobi and served as librarian and Privatdozent at Bonn in 1920.

Wilt L. Idema is a sinologist who studied under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé at Leiden University (~1963–1974). He held a professorship at Leiden (1975–1999) and posts at Harvard University (~1999–2013) and the Radcliffe Institute (2001–2002).
Winfred Robert Martin (d. 1915) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who studied at Cornell (~1967–1971). She held posts at Washington and Lee University, the University of Chicago (~2000–2005), and Indiana University (~2012).
Winston Kyan is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung, attested in 2006.

Wolfgang Morgenroth (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1976–1995) and the University of Potsdam (2020).
